prompt:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam and Max together: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora) and Max, the white rabbit-like creature (long ears, wide toothy grin, no clothes). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (6 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 296 to 344 pixels tall and from 328 to 340 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig223_05/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


SELECTED ATLAS PRODUCTION PASS. The text above is the preserved complete-job-sheet brief. For THIS call, Image 1 is a selected atlas of complete source drawings. Render ONLY its selected drawings in the same cells, at the exact same size, proportions and location. Do not generate the entire original job sheets. Image 2 is Sam's approved master and Image 3 is Max's approved master, used only for identity, original local colors and clean Purcell drawing style. Image 1 is the only pose and geometry reference. Output one 1536 x 1024 RGBA PNG with real transparent background, no magenta, checkerboard, white or black fill, labels, grid, floor, shadow or glow. Leave every drawing wholly inside its cell with clear separation. Smooth clean anti-aliased hand-drawn contours with controlled varied line weight, flat source colors, a few source-matched shadows. No pixel steps, texturing, gradients or generic added detail.

Verified original game context: costume223, palette0, room45, Conroy's bedroom, local primary script210. This complete drawing contains BOTH Sam AND Max AND the large OPEN BOOK together. Max is flattened low with the pale cream parts and pink ear strips spread around the gray-blue open book, as drawn in the original. Sam stands beside him, ponders with one hand under his muzzle, gestures and later crouches to read the book. These strange proportions and positions are deliberate cartoon poses. The book is not clothing or a blanket; preserve its open two-page silhouette and the source's small gray page marks without inventing words. Keep the exact source overlap, finger and foot contacts, bent limbs, nose orientation, hat, lapels, striped tie and bare brown feet. Preserve the concealed areas and all small white/pink shapes literally. Do not complete Max into a normal upright rabbit, invent a new visible face or grin under the book, add a third character, move the book, or replace either figure's pose with the master-sheet pose. The extra ordinary upright Max visible in the source game context is a separate unchanged actor and is NOT part of this asset. No game background is part of this painting. The first image's poses, including Sam's actual facing direction, override the generic facing/start-pose labels of the preserved brief above.

Cell 1: costume223_1947, cell rectangle [0, 0, 512, 1024], visible drawing top-left [86, 344], size [340, 336] pixels. Copy this exact complete two-character pose and book as one painting.

Cell 2: costume223_1948, cell rectangle [512, 0, 512, 1024], visible drawing top-left [600, 352], size [336, 320] pixels. Copy this exact complete two-character pose and book as one painting.

Cell 3: costume223_1949, cell rectangle [1024, 0, 512, 1024], visible drawing top-left [1116, 364], size [328, 296] pixels. Copy this exact complete two-character pose and book as one painting.

IMPORTANT PER-CELL POSE SEQUENCE: Left cell costume223_1947: Sam still STANDS UPRIGHT, both arms low, image-left hand bent only at waist height, image-right hand by thigh. Center cell costume223_1948: Sam BENDS HIS KNEES and lowers his whole upper body toward the book; his image-left hand reaches toward the book, his other hand is near the bent knee. Right cell costume223_1949: Sam is DEEPLY CROUCHED on bent legs, his head and shoulders visibly lower than in the center cell, one hand reaching over/beside the book and the other low near his feet. These three different body heights and arm positions are mandatory. None has a hand under the chin or by the face. Copy the three distinct source silhouettes exactly. The book and flattened Max stay in place below.
